report:
**Conclusion:** The health claim is **true**. Bystander hands-only (chest-compression-only) CPR is strongly associated with higher survival rates following an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) compared to receiving no bystander CPR.

### Key Evidence Summary

* **Higher Survival Odds:** Data from health organizations show that performing hands-only CPR approximately doubles a victim's chance of survival compared to taking no action (https://www.emergency-live.com/health-and-safety/survive-an-ohca-the-american-heart-association-revealed-that-hands-only-cpr-increases-survival-rate/).
* **Comparative Clinical Outcomes:** Observational studies analyzing OHCA outcomes demonstrate significantly higher rates of survival to hospital discharge for individuals who receive compression-only CPR (e.g., 13.3%) compared to those who receive no CPR (e.g., 5.2%) (https://www.the-hospitalist.org/hospitalist/article/124828/literature-research-you-need-know).
* **Increased Intervention Rates:** Promoting hands-only CPR lowers psychological and technical barriers for untrained lay bystanders. This leads to faster initiation of chest compressions, fewer interruptions, and increased overall bystander intervention, which directly translates to improved survival rates (https://www.lutheranhomessc.org/blog/compression-only-cpr-increases-survival-out-hospital-cardiac-arrest).

Prompt bystander chest compressions maintain crucial blood circulation to vital organs until professional emergency medical services arrive, making hands-only CPR far superior to no intervention.
